# flyee.club — Platform monorepo

The PLATFORM of flyee.club: accounts, billing (Asaas for BRL, Stripe for USD), entitlements, member token issuance with 30-day revalidation, the package-delivery API the `npx flyee` CLI consumes, catalog and release management, the member dashboard, admin consoles, per-segment metrics, the waitlist and the bilingual public site. The PRODUCT (the CLI, the harness core and the module contents) is a separate project that consumes this platform's API contract and module manifest; it never lives here. This repo has no link to any template: it was copied from the MedChina codebase on 2026-09-30 and is being reshaped into the platform phase by phase.

## Where things stand

- Plan and progress: `docs/PLANO-IMPLEMENTACAO.md` (phases 0–8 done; phases 9 and 10 were planned on 2026-10-06 and are not built: the free rung by version channel, the content funnel, the manifest v2 for pipelines and automation, the service token and index import, `/instalar.md`, compatibility tiers, the read-only MCP door and the anti-resale measures; phase 11, support with an integrated AI agent (including the brief's per-app questions), comes last, once the platform is complete; the "Andamento" table says what is done). Product decisions and open questions: `docs/PRODUCT.md` ("Decisões tomadas 2026-09-30" and "Decisões tomadas 2026-10-06").
- Done: phase 0 (identity, two locales, de-templated harness), phase 1 (clinical code, mobile app and dead packages removed), phase 2 (the database baseline), phase 7.1 (path-based locales for the public site), the code of the first-deploy milestone (bilingual waitlist with double opt-in, legal pages from `consent_terms`, launch stage and company line managed at `/admin/support`), phase 4 (the billing ladder: kit, membership and Pro, in BRL through Asaas and USD through Stripe, `docs/BILLING.md`), phase 3 (the CLI token server, the `/api/cli/*` delivery API, the module manifest and the package upload, `docs/CLI-CONTRACT.md`), phase 5 (the member dashboard: home, tools, recipes, news, meetings, roadmap, devices, onboarding), the official brand (logo, Londrina Solid and JetBrains Mono, provisional orange palette), phase 6 (the admin consoles: members, metrics with the focus rule, catalog, roadmap, meetings, leads, and the Monday digest) and phases 7.2 and 7.3 (the public pages: the full home, how it works, the public catalog and module pages, about and the founders offer; visits counted per entry door; the Pixel and GA4 in the member area with version 2 of the privacy and cookie policies; the SEO and tracking docs rewritten) and phase 8 (every e-mail in both languages, the bell written in each member's language, the scheduled jobs, messages to the confirmed list and the unsubscribe flow; `docs/DEPLOY.md`, "E-mails e jobs"). Every phase of the plan is done. What is left is the deploy itself, which waits on the new services and the company data (`docs/DEPLOY.md`, "Primeiro deploy").
- **The database is the flyee.club baseline** (`packages/db/migrations`, `0000`–`0018`, plus the migrations added on top through `0023_messages`, with the pgTAP suite in `packages/db/tests`). It has not been applied to a hosted project yet: that happens once the new Supabase project exists (`npm run db:gate:remote`). New schema work is a new numbered migration on top of it. See `packages/db/README.md`.

## Safety during the transition

- `apps/web/.env` is inherited and holds **MedChina production credentials** (Supabase, Asaas, Meta, GA4, AI keys). `apps/web/.env.local` blanks every one of them and must stay in place until the new flyee.club services exist. Next.js loads `.env.local` first, so the blank wins.
- Never run `db:plan:remote`, `db:migrate:remote`, `db:gate:remote` or `test:db:remote` until `.env.local` points at the new flyee.club Supabase project. The gate (`scripts/remote-db-gate.mjs`) reads `.env.local` first, bootstraps an EMPTY project, and refuses a database it did not build (the MedChina one included, whose history names files this repo does not have), but do not lean on that.
- Never commit `.env` or `.env.local`. Commit per plan phase, never push without being asked.

## Product (summary of docs/PRODUCT.md)

- **What it is**: a club called FlyeeClub, sold as a one-time access (the plan called "FlyeeClub") plus a subscription ("FlyeeClub Pro"). Members install the flyee harness in the AI they already use (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor) and keep receiving versioned tool modules and the updates that keep them working when the AIs change. The club never spends AI credit on the member's behalf.
- **Ladder** (prices are hypotheses stored as data in `plans`, never in code): the free rung (an account with no purchase, reached only through content; it installs the entry version of each app and is never sold or advertised) → FlyeeClub (tier `kit`: one-time, a year of catalog and updates counted from the paid invoice, renewed by buying again, card installments in BRL, 1 device; what every CTA sells) → FlyeeClub Pro (tier `club`: monthly or annual: advanced lessons, recipes, meetings, roadmap vote, the "open the hood" depth, 3 devices) → mentoring and consulting, sold on demand through the contact form, never as plans. The former Pro family (`pro-*`) is inactive since migration 0025, kept for history. Every paid plan may be used in client projects; refunds go through support.
- **Delivery**: the dashboard issues the member token; `npx flyee` installs and updates from the platform's package server. Every update rotates the token; after 30 days without an update the member revalidates in the dashboard, which is where the next tier is offered. Installed tools keep working when access ends; only updates stop.
- **Catalog**: one icon per module, filtered by seven stages (Planejar, Construir, Publicar, Divulgar, Vender, Escalar, Manter). The public store (the home and `/catalogo`) filters by store categories instead, the kinds of work of the home brief (Vender, Divulgar, Vídeo, Pesquisa, Construir): data edited in `/admin/catalogo` (`catalog_store_categories`, migration 0029), never in a manifest. The member area, the roadmap, the broad-use rule and the CLI API stay on the stages. Example: the video-editing app is in the stage Divulgar and the category Vídeo. Each app also carries the personas it is a good start for (`catalog_modules.personas`, migration 0032, marked in the console): the home brief's "Para quem é" block shows up to three published apps per persona (`lib/catalog/starters.ts`). Each module page carries a written guide in pt-BR and EN (how to use it, and the "open the hood" depth for FlyeeClub Pro), shipped inside each version's package at `guides/<pt-BR|en>/<usar|abrir-o-capo>.md` and shown for the version the member has installed, with an optional short video (unlisted YouTube); plus versions, changelog, declared permissions and checksum.
- **Metrics**: usage events only, never content, dimensioned by segment (`negocio`, `agencia`, `produto`, `dev`, `outro`: the public site's personas plus "other", migration 0028), AI tool and language. The focus segment is chosen by a data rule, not a date.
- **Free rung by version** (decided 2026-10-06, phase 9, not built yet): entitlement becomes per version through channels. The free plan is on channel `free` and gets only the version of each app marked free in the console (the first published one by default); kit, membership and Pro stay on `latest`. The free version is never updated because no new version enters `free`, not because of a block. The catalog answers `latest` per channel and `newest` for everyone, so the distance is visible in the CLI and in the dashboard.
- **The product repo** is `C:\AppsProjects\flyee`: the public npm package `flyee` (the CLI; 1.x supersedes an unrelated 0.7.x line the operator owns), the harness core bundled in it, and the apps, which are ZIPs uploaded to this platform, never npm packages. Its canonical harness file is `AGENTS.md` with `CLAUDE.md`/`GEMINI.md` pointers, and skills in `.agents/skills` bridged into `.claude/skills`. The first app is a video-editing app.
- **Pipelines, compatibility and the MCP door** (decided 2026-10-06, phase 10, not built): a `workflow` app is a packaged pipeline whose automatic half runs locally without approvals and whose on-demand half takes the decisions; the platform never runs anything. The core keeps a declarative registry of AI tools with two tiers, "tested" (`compatible_ais`) and "compatible by the standard" (`AGENTS.md` + `.agents/skills`, reported as `other`, promoted by data). Every app ships an eval that also runs as a nightly canary. A read-only remote MCP server on the platform and a local one in the CLI are planned. Anti-resale (confirmed 2026-10-06): a signed per-download license binds the harness to the account and machine, generated files carry an opaque account mark, downloads are watched for anomalies, and the terms forbid redistribution; skills are never encrypted and installed apps never stop working.

## Structure

- `apps/web` — Next.js 15 (App Router) + React 19 + MUI v9 + MUI X Premium + Tailwind 4, deployed on Vercel. See `apps/web/CLAUDE.md`.
  - **Member dashboard** (`app/(dashboard)`): `/inicio` (the member's rung, the install block with machines and the revalidation date, the activation checklist, latest releases, an offer when `lib/upsell.ts` says so), `/modulos` and `/modulos/[slug]` (the catalog, lessons, permissions, releases), `/receitas`, `/novidades`, `/encontros`, `/roadmap` (the votes, the proposals of FlyeeClub Pro members into a queue the operator reviews, the month's most voted idea, and the contact route for a commissioned app), `/settings` (profile, segment, AI tool, language, security and 2FA, devices, billing), plus the three-step wizard at `/onboarding`. Each screen is a server page that loads data with the member's session (`lib/member/*`) and a view that takes plain props. Screens are goal-first, never CRUD by default; quality is enforced by the `product-screen` skill (loaded by `.claude/hooks/product-screen-guard.mjs`, which also injects `components/product/catalog.json`), the `product-lint` hook and the `product-verify` skill.
  - **Admin** (`app/(dashboard)/admin`, superadmin only): overview; the club's consoles — `/admin/membros` (accounts, rungs, machines, the dossier and every action on an account), `/admin/metricas` (the five focus metrics per segment and week, the focus rule, entry doors), `/admin/catalogo` (tools, version upload and publishing, lessons, recipes, trails, delivery settings), `/admin/roadmap` (the queue under review, the month's leader to plan), `/admin/encontros`, `/admin/leads`; then billing, AI model prices, audit, insights, backups, announcements, help, blog and news, site and support. Each console is a server page that reads with the operator's session (`lib/admin/*`, `loadConsole`) and a client view; writes are server actions that check the role again and audit. A Monday digest (`lib/admin-jobs.ts`) rings and e-mails the operators. Admin copy is hardcoded pt-BR.
  - **Public site** (`app/[locale]/(marketing)`): the home, `/como-funciona`, `/catalogo` and `/catalogo/[slug]` (published modules, read-only), `/planos`, `/sobre`, `/contato`, `/ajuda`, `/blog`, the waitlist (`/espera`), the checksum page (`/verificar/[ref]`) and the legal pages rendered from `consent_terms`, composed from `components/marketing/*`, in Portuguese at `/` and in English at `/en` with translated addresses (`src/i18n/routing.ts`). Campaign pages without the site menu live in `app/[locale]/(funil)` (`/fundadores`, `noindex`). Until the launch stage is `open`, every primary CTA leads to the waitlist. Every number on a public page comes from the database. Quality is enforced by the `marketing-page` skill (loaded by `.claude/hooks/marketing-guard.mjs`) and the `marketing-lint` hook, both covering the two groups.
  - **Checkout and auth**: `/assinatura`, `/auth/*`, billing webhooks at `/api/webhooks/[provider]`.
  - **CLI connection and delivery** (`docs/CLI-CONTRACT.md`): the OAuth 2.1 server for the first-party `flyee-cli` client (`/oauth/authorize` with its revalidation variant, `/ativar` for device codes, `/revalidar`, `/api/oauth/{token,device,revoke}`), the delivery API `/api/cli/*` (every call walks `lib/cli/gates.ts`: token → scope → entitlement → device → rate), the package upload `/api/admin/catalog/{uploads,versions}` and the public checksum page `/verificar/[ref]`.
- `packages/design-tokens` — design system source of truth: the provisional palette in `css/orange.css` (`theme-orange`), neutrals and the deep band (`--background-deep`) in `css/common.css`, `css/marketing.css` (fluid display scale, section rhythm, motion). See its README.
- `packages/db` — the SQL baseline with RLS on every table and explicit grants (one organization per member: the personal workspace), the pgTAP suite, and a Drizzle mirror generated from the migrations. See its README.
- `packages/auth` — Supabase clients (browser/server/middleware/service), 2FA step-up, and the parallel session cookie used by support impersonation.
- `packages/billing` — the ladder (the kit as a one-time access purchase; membership and Pro, monthly and yearly; every plan in BRL and in USD), subscriptions with price snapshots, entitlement grants, coupons, invoices; Asaas (BRL) and Stripe (USD) behind one `PaymentProvider`, routed by the plan's currency. Pure, client-safe helpers in `@flyee/billing/currency` and `@flyee/billing/entitlements`. See `docs/BILLING.md`.
- `packages/email` — Resend + React Email (server-only): one sender per message, the templates and their copy in both languages (`src/copy/pt-BR.ts` is the structural source). No sender throws, and all no-op without `RESEND_API_KEY`, so callers keep a path that works without e-mail. See its README.
- `packages/jobs` — Inngest client + typed event map; functions live next to the code they run (`apps/web/src/lib/*-jobs.ts`, a package's `src/jobs.ts`) and are served by `apps/web` at `/api/inngest`. `sendEvent` never throws; callers fall back to inline work. Jobs that write to people follow claim-then-send (its README).
- `packages/audit` — append-only `audit_events`, the `access_events` sign-in trail, row versioning, versioned consent terms and acceptances.
- `packages/backup` — nightly logical backups of every `public` table, plus on demand from `/admin/backups`.
- `packages/ai` — chat providers (Anthropic/Gemini/OpenRouter) behind one interface, used by `/admin/insights`; usage feeds the `ai_spend` ledger.
- `packages/fields` — pure validators/formatters/masks (phone, CPF/CNPJ, CEP, currency; persist digits) + the ViaCEP lookup provider.
- `packages/onboarding` — activation state machinery; the steps live in `apps/web/src/lib/onboarding.ts`.
- `packages/content` — `BRAND` (site identity) + the message catalogs `messages/{pt-BR,en}.json`. The official brand art (the SVGs, as delivered) lives in `apps/web/public/brand/`; every raster is derived from the mark by `npm run brand:assets -w @flyee/web`.
- `packages/catalog` — the `flyee.module.json` manifest schema (zod, published as JSON Schema at `/api/cli/schema/module`) and the catalog's version rules, shared by the upload pipeline and the delivery API.
- `docs/` — `PRODUCT.md`, `PLANO-IMPLEMENTACAO.md`, `DEPLOY.md`, `DESIGN.md` (provisional direction), `HOME-COPY.md` (the home copy the product owner delivered), `ASAAS-GO-LIVE.md`, `BILLING.md` (the billing design), `CLI-CONTRACT.md` (the contract the CLI builds against), `BILLING-AUDIT.md` (historical), `SEO.md` and `TRACKING.md` (rewritten in phase 7).
- `attachments/` — input inbox: drop project material here; agents route each file to its canonical home per `attachments/README.md`.

## Golden rules

- **Platform, not product.** Never add CLI, harness or module logic here. The product exists in this repo only as the `/api/cli/*` contract and the module manifest schema.
- **Configurable data, never constants**: prices, plan limits, device ceilings, rate limits, grace windows, guarantee days and trial lengths live in `plans` and `platform_settings`.
- **The free rung is never offered.** No button, price column, badge or copy sells a free plan or a "free account" anywhere (no "Assine grátis", no "Criar conta gratuita"), and public pages never advertise free versions or free samples. The account with no purchase is the by-product of a sign-up that came from content (a video link carrying `origem`) or from the installer's no-login message; inside the member area it is described by what it is ("sem acesso ao catálogo", "versão de entrada"), never as a named plan.
- **Copy rules** (decided 2026-10-07): no dash (— or –), exclamation mark or emoji in any text a visitor or member reads, in both languages (site, member area, checkout, e-mails, bell, CLI messages, legal texts; © and → stay), and none of the banned words (desbloqueie, potencialize, sem esforço, soluções inovadoras; unlock, elevate, empower, seamless, robust, supercharge, game-changing, "it's not just"). The operator console is exempt. Enforced by `apps/web/src/lib/i18n/copy-rules.test.ts`, pgTAP `0033_copy_rules` and the e2e text check (`.claude/rules/marketing.md`).
- **Honest metrics**: `product_events` records usage, never content, through one allowlist of names and property values; segment, locale and AI tool are stamped from the profile on the server, never trusted from the client.
- Every mutation records an audit event (`recordAudit` in `apps/web/src/lib/audit.ts`). Every table has RLS, and every new migration states its grants explicitly.
- Visual identity changes ONLY in `packages/design-tokens/css/*.css`; run `npm run tokens:generate` and commit `tokens.generated.ts` with it.
- npm workspaces: install dependencies from the root (`npm install`), never inside an app.
- Icons: Phosphor through the tsconfig alias `@/icons/nexture/*` → `src/icons/phosphor/*` (fallback stubs re-export Nexture).
- Fonts: Mulish (`--font-body`), Londrina Solid (`--font-heading`; `font-display` falls back to it) and JetBrains Mono (`--font-mono`). Londrina Solid has two weights, Regular and Black: Black (`font-bold`) for the display scale and headings from 24px up, Regular (`font-normal`) below that.
- The dark band (footer, deep sections, terminal bodies) is `bg-background-deep`, never the dark primary: it has to stay dark under any palette.
- Red is reserved for risk and failure.

## Shared Claude/Codex harness

- `CLAUDE.md`, `apps/web/CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/*`, `.claude/skills/*` and `.claude/hooks/*` are the canonical shared sources. They are the platform's development harness: nothing in them is distributed to members. Do not maintain a second hand-written Codex copy.
- Codex reads the generated `AGENTS.md` mirror and the generated `.agents/skills/*` bridges. `.codex/config.toml` points its lifecycle hooks at the same implementations under `.claude/hooks/`.
- `PostToolUse` runs `scripts/sync-agent-harness.mjs` after canonical harness edits. `npm run harness:check` and `npm run harness:test` also run in the pre-commit hook.

## Commands (root)

- `npm run dev` / `build` / `start` / `lint` / `lint:fix` / `prettier` — delegate to `apps/web`.
- `npm run typecheck` — `apps/web` with its pinned TypeScript 5.8. Never run a bare root `npx tsc` on apps/web: it picks the hoisted TS 6.
- `npm run test` — `@flyee/ai` node tests + the web vitest suite. `npm run test:e2e` / `test:a11y` — Playwright against a production build.
- `npm run ci:verify` — everything CI runs: harness checks, MUI class check, typecheck, tests, build.
- `node scripts/prune-messages.mjs --check|--write|--list` — message catalogs without unused or missing keys (pt-BR is the reference).
- `npm run test:db:embedded` — migrations + pgTAP on an embedded PostgreSQL 17, no Docker (first run installs it into `.cache/`). `npm run db:start` / `db:stop` / `test:db` — the same through local Supabase (needs Docker). The `db:*:remote` scripts are gated: see "Safety during the transition".
- `npm run db:schema:pull` — regenerate the Drizzle mirror from the migrations.
- `npm run tokens:generate` — regenerate the TS token mirror.

## Platform decisions

- Deploy: Vercel, only through GitHub Actions (`docs/DEPLOY.md`). Database, auth and storage: Supabase (Postgres + RLS). ORM: Drizzle. Email: Resend. Jobs and cron: Inngest. Billing: Asaas for BRL (PIX, card, Asaas issues the NFS-e) and Stripe for USD, routed by the purchase currency.
- Locales: pt-BR (default) and en, hybrid since phase 7.1: the public site lives under `app/[locale]` with next-intl `pathnames` (pt-BR at `/`, English at `/en` with translated paths, both indexed with hreflang), while dashboard, admin, auth and checkout keep the cookie and profile locale.
- Guides are written and travel in each version's package (migration 0030, `docs/CLI-CONTRACT.md` §7), read through `can_read_guide`; the optional video of a guide is an unlisted YouTube video gated by the page and by RLS (`can_watch_lesson`). Meetings use an external link (Zoom/Meet), with registration and click-through recorded on the platform.
- Do not introduce Cloudflare-specific services (Workers, D1, R2, Workers AI).

This repo stays **private**: the UI layer contains commercially licensed code (MUI X Premium license and the Nexture template components).

===== apps/web/CLAUDE.md =====

# flyee.club web (apps/web)

Next.js 15 (App Router) + React 19 — the only app of the flyee.club platform: public site, member dashboard, checkout, admin consoles and the CLI delivery API. See the root `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/PRODUCT.md` and `docs/PLANO-IMPLEMENTACAO.md`.

> The database is the baseline in `packages/db/migrations` (`0000`–`0018`, plus the migrations added since, described in `packages/db/README.md`). Prefer the function name when searching for a rule.

## Stack and conventions

- **UI**: MUI v9 is the base. Before building a component, look for a MUI or MUI X equivalent (installed: Data Grid + Pro, Charts + Pro, Date Pickers, Tree View, Lab). Icons: **Phosphor** through the `@/icons/nexture/*` tsconfig alias (real adapters plus Nexture fallback stubs, see `src/icons/README.md`); never import an icon library directly. Import the one icon you render; `src/icons/icon-registry.tsx` (icons by NAME, for the dashboard menu and catalog icons) imports the whole set and ships all of it to any client component that imports it.
- **Styling**: MUI theme driven by CSS variables (`hsl(var(--token))`) from `@flyee/design-tokens`. Component overrides live in `src/style/**/*.css` inside CSS layers (`theme, base, mui, components, utilities`). Tailwind 4 for layout utilities, merged with `tailwind-merge`. Run `npm run check:mui-classes` after touching `src/style/**`.
- **Themes**: one locked palette (`theme-orange`, provisional) × light/dark, as classes on `<html>`. The tokens are scoped to those classes, so the root layout renders them on the server (the palette and the default mode) and a script in `<head>` corrects the mode before the first paint for a browser that stored another choice; `src/theme/theme-provider.tsx` keeps them in sync afterwards and applies only a palette listed in `THEME_OPTIONS` whatever a browser has stored. Never leave the classes to a client effect again: until it ran, the page had no palette at all. Fonts: Mulish (`--font-body`), Londrina Solid (`--font-heading`; `font-display` falls back to it) and JetBrains Mono (`--font-mono`, every `<code>`/`<pre>` and `font-mono`). Londrina Solid ships Regular and Black only: MUI `h1`/`h2` and the display scale are Black, `h3`–`h6` and any heading under 24px are Regular (`font-normal`).
- **Forms**: Formik + Yup. Semantic data (phone, CPF/CNPJ, CEP, money) uses `components/product/fields/*`, never a raw `TextField`; persist digits, never masks.
- **i18n**: next-intl; every user-facing string goes through messages. Locales `pt-BR` (default) and `en`; catalogs in `packages/content/messages/`. `src/lib/i18n/messages.test.ts` pins key parity, no blank values and identical ICU placeholders. `node scripts/prune-messages.mjs --check` fails on keys no code renders and on keys the code renders that the catalog lacks. Namespaces: `marketing` (public site), `auth`, `product` (member dashboard, billing, settings), `dashboard` (chrome and menu). The home's copy lives in `components/marketing/home-copy/{pt-BR,en}.ts`; `pt-BR.ts` is the structural source of truth (`HomeCopy = typeof homeCopyPtBR`); the text follows `docs/HOME-COPY.md`, the home copy the product owner delivered.
- **Admin copy is hardcoded pt-BR**, outside i18n: the operator surface has one reader. Code comments stay in English; a database value (enum, slug, status) is mapped to a label, never shown raw. `components/data-grid/data-table.tsx` takes its grid chrome from MUI X's own locale pack.
- **Which language a request is in** depends on the kind of page, and `i18n/request.ts` is the one place that decides it:
  - **Public site: the URL.** Pages live under `app/[locale]/` (Portuguese at `/`, English at `/en` with translated addresses) and are declared in `src/i18n/routing.ts` (next-intl `pathnames`, `localeDetection: false`). The middleware runs next-intl only for those addresses (`matchPublicPath`), merging the refreshed Supabase cookies into its rewrite, and persists the URL language in the locale cookie so sign-in and the app that follow continue in it. Internal links use `LocaleLink`/`localizeHref` with the Portuguese path; `app/[locale]/layout.tsx` repeats the `NextIntlClientProvider` because the root layout is not re-rendered by a client-side navigation; the public language switch is a full page load. A browser that reads the other language gets an offer (`language-suggestion.tsx`), never a redirect.
  - **Everything else (sign-in, member area, checkout, admin): the visitor.** `lib/locale-request.ts` (`resolveRequestLocale`): the cookie is the visitor's choice and always wins; otherwise `lib/locale-detection.ts` decides from `Accept-Language`, then Vercel's `x-vercel-ip-country`. Three rules are load-bearing: detection happens at RENDER time, not only in the middleware (a cookie set by the middleware lands on the response); a crawler is never switched (`isCrawler`); an automatic switch is always announced (`COOKIE_KEYS.localeAuto`). The in-app switch (`setClientLocale` in `i18n/locale.ts`) also writes `profiles.locale` through `update_member_profile`, outside support sessions; a new browser does not read the profile yet (detection decides until the member switches).
- **Path alias**: `@/*` → `./src/*`. **Brand**: identity comes from `@flyee/content` (`src/brand.ts` re-exports it); the logo is the single component `src/components/logo/logo.tsx`, which references the official SVGs in `public/brand/` (light-surface and dark-surface files; `tone="contrast"` on the deep band) and never redraws them. The favicons, the square mark and the home-screen tile are generated from the mark: `npm run brand:assets`.
- **Remote data**: `lib/remote-state.ts` (`RemoteState<T>`: idle, loading, success, empty, error). An error is never rendered as empty.

## Member dashboard (product layer)

- Routes: `/inicio` (`DEFAULTS.appRoot`), `/modulos` and `/modulos/[slug]` (the dashboard catalog is `/modulos` because the public one is `/catalogo`), `/receitas` and `/receitas/[slug]`, `/novidades`, `/encontros` and `/encontros/[slug]`, `/roadmap`, `/settings` (profile and avatar, segment, AI tool, language, timezone, credentials), `/settings/security` (2FA, sign-in history), `/settings/devices` (machines, revalidation dates, disconnect; `/settings/connections` redirects here), `/settings/billing`, and `/onboarding` (outside the dashboard shell).
- **Screen shape**: `page.tsx` is a server component that reads with the member's session through `lib/member/*` (`getMemberContext()` gives the session client, workspace, language, currency and `org_entitlements`; the catalog comes from `lib/catalog/read.ts`, shared with the CLI API) and hands a `state` (`ready` | `error` | `unavailable`) to a client view that takes plain props. An error is never rendered as an empty state, and every write goes through `lib/member/actions.ts` to the database function that owns the rule.
- **Guides** (`lib/member/guides.ts`, `components/product/guide-panel.tsx`, migration 0030): each version's package carries its written guides (`guides/<pt-BR|en>/<usar|abrir-o-capo>.md`, `@flyee/catalog/guides`); the upload stores which guides a version carries (`catalog_module_versions.guides`, public) and their text (`catalog_guides`, read through `can_read_guide`: the basic depth with the app's entitlement, "abrir o capô" with `advanced_lessons`). The member's app page shows the guide of the version installed on their machines (else the newest with a guide) and says when a newer one is out; a guide the version carries but the query did not return is the lock. The depth's video sits inside the guide: its id is only returned when `can_watch_lesson` allows it, the player loads youtube-nocookie on play and records `lesson.started` / `lesson.completed`.
- **Offers** (`lib/upsell.ts`, `decideUpsell` and `decideServiceOffers`): no access → FlyeeClub; FlyeeClub → FlyeeClub Pro (the reason is the broad use when three or more trails were used in 30 days, plain membership otherwise); every paying member also sees the services sold on demand (mentoring, consulting), which lead to `/contato?assunto=`. Nothing offers the retired Pro. The card (`UpsellCard`) appears on the home and on the CLI revalidation screen, says why it is there and shows the price from `plans`; the billing webhook records `upsell.purchased` when a purchase follows a card seen in the last 14 days.
- **Roadmap** (`lib/member/community.ts`, `/roadmap`, migration 0026): everyone reads; a FlyeeClub Pro member (`roadmap_vote`) votes and proposes through `propose_roadmap_item`, into a queue under review (`submitted`) that only the author and the operator see, capped by `platform_settings.roadmap.max_open_proposals`; `/admin/roadmap` opens a proposal for votes or declines it. `roadmap_month_leader(month)` names the open idea with the most votes cast in the month: the tile on the member's roadmap and what the operator plans at the turn of the month. A commissioned app is the contact form (`/contato?assunto=app`), never a quote or a payment here. "Próximos na loja" (migration 0033, `lib/roadmap-coming-next.ts`): planning the month's leader from the console records `won_month`, the operator marks a paid request `commissioned`, and `roadmap_coming_next()` is the only part of the roadmap a visitor reads (planned and building ideas, one badge each).
- **Activation** (`lib/onboarding.ts`): four steps with LIVE predicates, never click tracking — profile (segment, AI tool, language) → access (kit or plan) → install (`npx flyee login`) → first run (closed by the CLI's first `tool.executed`). The facts come from the definer RPC `member_activation_facts()`. `isActivated` = a device AND a first execution. `resolvePostAuthDestination` (called by sign-in, sign-up, `/auth/callback` and `/auth/two-factor`; never from the middleware) sends a member to the `/onboarding` wizard only while the profile questions are unanswered; the later steps are the home's checklist.
- **Entitlements**: `hooks/use-entitlements.ts` calls `org_entitlements(org)`, the single answer to what a workspace may use: the free floor, live grants (the kit, licenses, courtesies), the live subscription with its add-ons, and an unconfirmed PIX inside its window, merged so more sources never mean fewer rights, with the tier and the sources named. Screens branch on it, never on plan names. `org_has_entitlement(org, key)` is the yes/no form for policies and gates. `components/product/gate-notice.tsx` renders the gate states (`available`, `loading`, `unknown` with retry, `blocked` with a reason). `components/layout/menu/plan-indicator.tsx` shows the tier and the upgrade path.
- **Sign-up**: one person is one account. `handle_new_user` creates the profile AND the personal workspace from `display_name`; the sign-up metadata also carries `locale` (the phase 2 trigger reads `display_name`, `segment`, `ai_tool`, `locale`). `/auth/complete-profile` is only the safety net for an account without a workspace.
- **Usage events**: the browser reports only offers shown and clicked (`trackOffer` in `lib/product-events.ts`, which terminates the PostgREST builder with `.then()`: a bare `void supabase.rpc(...)` never sends the request). Everything that counts toward a metric is written by the backend with `trackServerEvent` (`lib/product-events-server.ts`). The database stamps segment, language and AI tool from the profile and drops any property outside its allowlist.
- Reusable blocks live in `components/product/*` and are listed in `components/product/catalog.json` (injected by the `product-screen-guard` hook). Every zero-data view uses `EmptyState`.

## Public site (marketing layer)

- Routes in `src/app/[locale]/(marketing)/`, each in Portuguese and English: home `/` and `/en`, `/como-funciona` (`/en/how-it-works`), `/catalogo` and `/catalogo/[slug]` (`/en/catalog/...`), `/planos` (`/en/pricing`), `/sobre` (`/en/about`), `/contato` (`/en/contact`), `/ajuda` (`/en/help`), `/blog` (`/en/blog`), `/espera` (`/en/waitlist`), `/verificar/[ref]` (`/en/verify/...`, `noindex`), `/legal/{termos,privacidade,cookies}` (`/en/legal/{terms,privacy,cookies}`). Campaign pages live in the sibling group `src/app/[locale]/(funil)/`, whose layout drops the site menu and keeps the trackers, the cookie notice, the support widget and a legal-minimum footer: `/fundadores` (`/en/founders`, `noindex`), the founders price with the seats and deadline of `founders_offer()` and a page per closed reason. A new public page is declared there (both addresses; that is also what makes it public to the middleware), enters `src/app/sitemap.ts` when indexed (once per language, with alternates), and spreads `publicPageMetadata({ path, locale })` from `lib/seo.ts` into its `generateMetadata` (canonical, hreflang with `x-default`, Open Graph URL).
- ONE design system: pages compose the primitives in `src/components/marketing/` (`Section`/`Container`/`SectionHeader`, Hero, FeatureRows, RuledGrid, ProcessSteps, StoreGrid, AppStorePreview, BentoGrid, StatBand, PricingSection, Faq, Cta), listed in `components/marketing/catalog.json`. The inherited Landing DS is gone. `docs/DESIGN.md` holds the committed direction (the palette is provisional): no palette hue on small text, hues ride on icons, bars and fills.
- **No loading boundary above the public pages**: neither an `app/loading.tsx` nor a `<Suspense>` in the root layout. A boundary there starts the response before a page can call `notFound()` or `redirect()`, so a missing app answered 200 with `noindex` and a moved address got a meta refresh. Each signed-in area keeps its own boundary in its layout. The public 404 is `app/not-found.tsx` (marketing namespace, leads back to the site); the member area has `app/(dashboard)/not-found.tsx`.
- **The loader overlay is for the signed-in areas only.** `#initial-loader` (root layout, `public/initial-loader.{css,js}`) covers the page until the window load event, while the shell settles. A public page arrives complete and styled, so the root layout leaves the overlay out (`isPublicPageRequest()` in `lib/locale-request.ts`): with it, a phone showed a white screen for seconds over content that was already painted. Anything a public page decides in the browser and shows above the fold must be decided before the first paint, from `<head>` (the mode class, the language offer of `lib/language-offer.ts`), never after hydration. Next serves a 404 thrown by a page as an error document that React builds in the browser, which never runs the loader script; `InitialLoaderGuard` lifts the overlay there.
- **Performance of the public site** (measured 2026-10-01, Lighthouse, production build): desktop 93 to 98, mobile 52 to 67, SEO 100. What a public page still pays on a phone is the shared shell: MUI and its styling engine hydrate on every page (three whole-document restyles at start-up) and one 382 KB stylesheet carries the overrides of every dashboard component. Getting the mobile score to 90 means a public shell without them, which is a decision, not a fix (`docs/PLANO-IMPLEMENTACAO.md`, phase 7). Do not add to that cost: no scripted animation, no client component where a server one does, one icon import per icon.
- **Public catalog** (`src/lib/catalog/public.ts`): `/catalogo`, the module pages, the numbers of the home and the module half of the sitemap read published rows with the anonymous client through the same reader as the CLI API (`lib/catalog/read.ts`). A module whose name has no English text stays out of the English pages and sitemap, and its English address leads to the English catalog; an unreadable catalog renders a "could not load" state, never an empty catalog.
- **Visits per entry door** (`src/lib/site-views.ts`): the middleware counts each document load of a public page by someone not signed in (never a crawler, a prefetch, a redirect or a client-side navigation) through `count_site_view`, after the response (`event.waitUntil`); the door is the link's `?origem=`, else the first-touch door. These are the visits of the entry doors table in `/admin/metricas`.
- `/ajuda` and `/blog` render DB-managed content (written in `/admin/help` and `/admin/blog`) through `src/lib/public-content.ts` (anon client, published rows, only in the language of the address: translations are rows linked by `translation_group`, and a slug of the other language redirects to its translation or to the section index); Markdown renders via `components/marketing/markdown-prose.tsx` (raw HTML ignored).
- **Legal pages render `consent_terms`** (`components/marketing/legal-document.tsx` over `lib/legal.ts`): the version in force of `terms`, `privacy` and `cookies` in the language of the address, with version and date, so the page shows exactly the text people accept. When the text cannot be read the page says so; the catalogs hold no second copy of the terms.
- **Launch stage** (`lib/launch.ts`, `platform_settings.launch`, migration 0019): in `waitlist` (the seed, and the fallback for anything unreadable) every primary CTA of the public site leads to `/espera`; in `open` they lead to sign-up and checkout. Sign-in and sign-up stay reachable in both. The superadmin flips it at `/admin/support`, which also holds the operating company printed in the footer (`legal_entity`, read by `getLegalEntity`): the terms identify the operator "in the site footer".
- **Waitlist** (`/espera`, `/en/waitlist`): `espera/actions.ts` validates (honeypot, consent), calls `submit_lead` with the service role (first-touch campaign from the attribution cookie, network window keyed by an HMAC of the IP with `PUBLIC_FORMS_IP_SALT`), and e-mails the double opt-in link (`sendLeadConfirmationEmail`, in the language the address signed up in). The answer never reveals whether an address was already listed. The link `/espera/confirmar?t=` is rewritten by the middleware: the token moves into an httpOnly cookie (`COOKIE_KEYS.leadConfirm`) and the page loads at the clean address, because analytics scripts and Referer headers carry URLs; confirming takes a button press, because mail scanners open every link. `lib/lead-jobs.ts` runs `purge_expired_leads` daily (unconfirmed addresses go after 7 days, as the page promises).
- Pricing reads plans through `@flyee/billing/public` (`listPublicPlans`, read-only) with i18n placeholder plans as fallback; the contact form sends through `@flyee/email` (`CONTACT_FORM_TO`).
- Display type: `font-display text-display-{2xl,xl,lg,md}` (fluid clamp scale from `@flyee/design-tokens/css/marketing.css`). Motion: CSS first (the hero entrance in `style/layout/marketing-motion.css`, `<Float>`, the `<Reveal>` transition started by `watchEntry` in `components/marketing/motion.ts`); GSAP is loaded only by `<Parallax>`, on demand, and never in admin code. Transform + opacity, honors `prefers-reduced-motion`, nothing runs forever.
- Site events (`lib/site-events.ts`, `docs/TRACKING.md`): the home brief's vocabulary (`cta_click`, `section_view`, `faq_open`, …) as GA4 and Pixel custom events, declared on elements with `data-track` / `trackAttributes()` and on sections with `track="<key>"`, reported by the one listener in `components/consent/marketing-analytics.tsx`; never a third tracker. The segment a visitor declares (`?segment=` or a click, `lib/site-segment.ts`) lives in a readable cookie and pre-fills the waitlist, the sign-up metadata and the onboarding; since migration 0028 the site's personas ARE `member_segment` (`negocio`, `agencia`, `produto`, `dev`, plus `outro`).
- Tracking (`docs/TRACKING.md`): the marketing and funnel layouts render the Meta Pixel and GA4 server-side; the member area loads the same snippets after the page is interactive and never on `/admin` (`components/consent/dashboard-trackers.tsx`); one opt-out cookie and one notice cover both (`lib/analytics.ts`, `CONSENT_VERSION` 4, privacy and cookie policies version 2 in migration 0022). Sign-up, checkout and purchase conversions also go server-side (`lib/meta-capi.ts`, `lib/ga4-mp.ts`). The snippets are written once in `lib/tracker-snippets.ts`.

## Billing and checkout

- `/settings/billing` (the ladder in the member's currency, current subscription, cancel with a reason and undo, invoices, billing profile, pending checkout, payment recovery) and `/assinatura?plan=<slug>` (the focused checkout; without `plan` it opens the kit in the visitor's currency; Pix, card or installments in BRL, Stripe Checkout in USD). Server actions in `settings/billing/actions.ts` (checkouts), `actions-cancel.ts` and `actions-recovery.ts`, sharing `billing-server.ts`; provider webhooks at `api/webhooks/[provider]/route.ts`, idempotent through `claim_billing_webhook_event`/`complete_billing_webhook_event` with an attempt ceiling.
- **Dunning grace**: `past_due` keeps access for a configurable window (`platform_settings` key `dunning`) counted from `subscriptions.past_due_since`; `billing_past_due_grace_ends()` is the one answer every gate shares. Installed tools always keep working; only updates stop.
- **Comped plans**: `set_org_plan(org, plan, note)` puts a workspace on a tier without checkout (betas, partners, the team). It updates the live row instead of inserting, keeps the period bounds NULL, refuses a provider-backed subscription (`provider_managed`) and stamps `self_grant` in the audit event when the operator comps their own account.
- The founders offer counts real seats (`lib/founders-offer.ts`); the guarantee window comes from `platform_settings` (`lib/guarantee.ts`); a pending PIX survives a closed tab (`lib/pending-pix.ts`).
- **Entitlements**: `org_entitlements(org)` is the one answer (free floor + live grants + live subscription + add-ons, with `tier` and `sources`). Screens read it through `hooks/use-entitlements.ts` and `@flyee/billing/entitlements`, never by plan name or slug. The kit is an `entitlement_grants` row the webhook creates on the paid invoice; CLI tokens are revoked only when catalog access really ends (`lib/billing-lifecycle.ts`).
- **Currency**: `?moeda=` (kept in a cookie by the middleware) or the page language picks BRL or USD (`lib/billing-currency.ts`), and the plan's currency picks the provider. A yearly BRL plan split into installments is ONE purchase that does not renew; so is the kit, which may also be split (`lib/payment-choice.ts`) and whose grant is keyed by the installment, not the parcel. The kit lasts `plans.access_months` from the paid invoice; buying it again chains a new term after the current one, the end is announced 15 days ahead and settled by the daily billing job (`lib/billing-notices.ts`). Full design, state machine, refunds and deferred items: `docs/BILLING.md`.

## Platform admin and account

- Superadmin area at `src/app/(dashboard)/admin`: `layout.tsx` is a server gate on `profiles.is_superadmin` (RLS stays the real defense); the Admin menu group renders only for superadmins (`hooks/use-is-superadmin.ts`). Consoles: `/admin` (the counters of `admin_metrics()` and a tile per console), `/admin/membros`, `/admin/metricas`, `/admin/catalogo` and `/admin/catalogo/[slug]`, `/admin/roadmap`, `/admin/encontros` and `/admin/encontros/[id]`, `/admin/leads`, `/admin/billing`, `/admin/ai` (model price book), `/admin/audit` (audit trail + sign-in log), `/admin/insights`, `/admin/backups`, `/admin/announcements`, `/admin/help`, `/admin/blog` (posts and member news, with audience and translation links), `/admin/support`. `/admin/organizations` redirects to `/admin/membros`.
- **Console shape** (phase 6): `page.tsx` is a server component that reads through `lib/admin/*` inside `loadConsole()` (`lib/admin/session.ts`: the operator's session, `ready | error | unavailable`, so a failed read is never an empty list) and hands plain props to a client view; writes are server actions in the console's `actions.ts` that call `requireSuperadmin()` again (a server action is a public endpoint) and record an audit event; the database function that owns the rule is the one doing the write wherever one exists. Formatting is `lib/admin/format.ts` (pt-BR, Brasília clock, money per currency, never summed) and every database value becomes a word through `lib/admin/labels.ts`.
- **Members** (`/admin/membros`, `admin_members_overview()` / `admin_member_dossier()`, migration 0015): the tiles are the filters and count the same flags the rows carry (`lib/admin/members.ts`). The dossier (row click) reads the account, its entitlements, money, machines, usage, consents and first touch. Actions: support access, disconnect every machine (`revoke_member_tokens`), reset 2FA, the superadmin role, ban (also revokes the CLI tokens: the token server is ours, not the auth provider's) and account deletion; ban, 2FA and deletion need `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`. A second tab lists people without a workspace.
- **Metrics** (`/admin/metricas`, `admin_segment_weekly()` with payers per currency and `admin_door_weekly()`, migrations 0015/0021): the focus rule (`focusRule` in `lib/admin/metrics.ts`) is the docs/PRODUCT.md proposal read as an indicator: a segment leads kit purchases, 7-day activation and weekly use for 4 COMPLETE weeks, comparing only the four focus segments with at least 30 accounts with access; `outro`, an unanswered segment and the running week never count; a tie or a blank week leads nobody. Windows still open (activation 7 d, kit to membership 60 d) are marked, never estimated.
- **Catalog** (`/admin/catalogo`): modules, recipes, trails (texts only: the seven slugs are fixed) and the delivery settings (`platform_settings.cli`). A module's page uploads the ZIP through the two-step upload of phase 3, then publishes, marks stable, yanks with a public reason or discards a draft (`lib/catalog/version-actions.ts`, `discardDraftVersion`); lessons keep the video id apart (`catalog_lesson_videos`). Usage per module and version comes from `admin_catalog_stats()` (migration 0021).
- **Meetings** (`/admin/encontros`): the lifecycle rascunho → inscrições → ao vivo → encerrado → arquivado, the page in both languages, the private room and recording links (`meeting_links`), results (`meeting_results`) and registrants (`admin_meeting_registrants`). The e-mails card shows how many registrants each of the four messages reached (confirmation, 24-hour reminder, last-hour reminder, recording) and sends one now, only inside its window (`meetingEmailWindow`), to whoever has not received it.
- **Leads** (`/admin/leads`): status tiles (confirmed, waiting, opted out), opt-out, erasure (`purge_lead`) and an export of confirmed, not opted-out contacts as a Resend contact CSV, audited. The newsletter consent covers e-mail sent through Resend only, so there is no ad-audience export. "Escrever para a lista" writes a message per language (Markdown), shows who would receive it before sending, and delivers it in batches (`newsletter_sends`, `lib/newsletter.ts`); a send that stopped is resumed from the same screen and never repeats a reader. Without an e-mail provider the screen says so and the button is off.
- Every mutation records an audit event through `lib/audit.ts` (`recordAudit`). Sign-ins are logged by a database trigger; members see their own in `/settings/security`.
- **Granting the superadmin role** (`set_user_superadmin(user, value, note)`): the flag is fenced by a trigger on `profiles` keyed on WHO is asking (`is_superadmin()` reads the database), because a self-`PATCH` of `is_superadmin` would otherwise promote any signed-in user. Self-change is refused in both directions. A session with no JWT (service role, migration, psql) passes: that is how the first superadmin is made.
- **Support impersonation** (`lib/impersonation-actions.ts`, started from `/admin/membros`, which a visit returns to): the operator works inside a member's account through a **parallel session cookie** (`@flyee/auth` `authCookieName`), so leaving deletes a cookie and never strands the operator. Load-bearing: the write fence is in the DATABASE (`is_impersonated()` matches the JWT `session_id` against `impersonation_sessions`; triggers refuse member-owned writes), and it never expires; ending a visit uses `signOut({ scope: "local" })`, never the global default; starting requires the operator's own session at AAL2; credentials and `/admin` are blocked in the middleware. A reason is required, the member is notified, and the access is labelled as support in their sign-in history. Duration lives in `platform_settings` (`impersonation`).
- **Account deletion** (`admin/membros/components/delete-account-dialog.tsx`, server action `deleteAccount`, RPC `admin_delete_account(user, confirm_email, reason)`): the unit is the account plus every workspace it alone belongs to. The order is fixed: re-read the preview, cancel any live provider subscription (a failure deletes nothing), run the RPC in one transaction (it deletes rows that hold data through NO ACTION/RESTRICT references first, holder before held, and purges `record_versions`), then remove storage files through the Storage API using `admin_orphaned_account_storage`, which refuses anything still alive. Refused in the database: yourself, any superadmin, a support session, a live provider subscription. The audit event `admin.account.deleted` survives with counts only.
- **AI spend** (`lib/ai-spend.ts`, price book at `/admin/ai`): every provider call records one `ai_spend` row through the `ChatProvider` `onUsage` sink. Prices are configuration (`platform_settings` key `ai_prices`, per million tokens), shipped empty; an unpriced model reports `priced = false`, and consoles show the unpriced count beside every total. Cost is stored in USD micros and converted only with an operator-set rate.
- `/admin/insights` (`api/admin/insights/route.ts`): the model writes SQL from an `information_schema` catalog and each statement runs inside a `read only` transaction with a 5 s `statement_timeout`. **The read-only transaction is the safety boundary, not the prompt.** Every executed query is audited and shown. Needs `DATABASE_URL` and one AI provider key.
- **Monday digest** (`lib/admin-jobs.ts` over `lib/admin/weekly-digest.ts`, Inngest cron at 08:30 Brasília): last complete week's five focus metrics per segment, the focus rule and the accounts that need someone (past due, cancellation scheduled, no update for 25 days, no machine), as one bell notification and one e-mail (`sendAdminWeeklyDigestEmail`) per superadmin. Nothing to report means nothing is sent; `notifications.source_key` (`admin-weekly:<week>`) makes it idempotent per week.
- `/admin/backups` (`@flyee/backup`): nightly cron plus "Run backup now" (inline fallback without Inngest). Archives land in the private `backups` bucket; downloads are signed URLs.
- Account plumbing is real: the header bell reads `notifications` (create rows server-side with `lib/notifications.ts`), announcements render in the dashboard layout with per-user dismissal, `/settings` edits the profile (avatar in the `avatars` bucket) and credentials. The quick-support widget (`components/support/support-widget.tsx`) reads the channels from `platform_settings` (`support`, edited at `/admin/support`), falls back to `BRAND.support`, and renders nothing until a human channel exists.

## Messages: bell, e-mail and scheduled jobs

- **Every message to a member is written in the reader's language**, chosen when it is written: `profiles.locale` for members, `leads.locale` for contacts of the list. Bell texts are stored text, so `notifyLocalized` (`lib/notifications.ts`) groups the recipients by language and takes the words from `lib/messages/bell-copy.ts`; e-mail copy lives in `packages/email/src/copy/{pt-BR,en}.ts`. Both are typed against the Portuguese object, so one language cannot gain a line the other lacks. Never write a member-facing sentence at a call site. The operator's own digests stay in Portuguese.
- **A plan is called by `plans.name`**, never by a word in the copy. A date and an amount arrive already formatted for the reader (`lib/messages/format.ts`: the reader's time zone, `America/Sao_Paulo` when unknown). A sentence that states a time ("within 24 hours") must be true anywhere inside the window the message is sent in (`lib/meeting-email-kinds.ts`).
- **Claim, then send.** A job that writes to people may run twice. The database marks the row in the statement that returns it (`claim_token_reminders`, `claim_term_end_notices`, `claim_meeting_emails`, `claim_newsletter_batch`, migration 0023) and only then the message leaves. Where there is no row to mark, the bell's unique `source_key` is the fence (the welcome, the weekly summary) and the e-mail goes only to who got a NEW bell row. A message may be lost to a failed send, never sent twice. A batch the provider refuses is given back (the meeting columns, `settle_newsletter_batch`), so the next run tries it again.
- **Without `RESEND_API_KEY` nothing breaks**: senders return `{ sent: false }` with no error, the bell still rings, and a job does not claim what exists only as e-mail (a meeting confirmation, a batch of the list). Without Inngest, what an action starts runs in the request (`requestMeetingEmails`, `startNewsletterDelivery`), and nothing scheduled runs.
- **What a reader can stop**: only the weekly summary (`profiles.marketing_email_opt_out`, the switch in `/settings`) and the messages to the list (`leads.opted_out_at`). Those carry `unsubscribeUrl(...)` in the body and as `List-Unsubscribe` (one click). `/api/public/email/unsubscribe` acts on POST only; a GET moves the request into an httpOnly cookie and lands on `/descadastro`, which asks with one button, because mail scanners open every link they deliver. Receipts, notices about the account and the reminders of a meeting someone registered for ignore the preference.
- **Jobs** live in `lib/*-jobs.ts` and are listed in `app/api/inngest/route.ts`; a function missing from that list never runs. `token-jobs` (a connection about to expire), `updates-digest-jobs` (weekly: only versions published that week, only machines with a live connection; the rule is `pendingUpdates` in `lib/updates-digest.ts`), `meeting-jobs` (a 10-minute sweep of `due_meeting_emails`, plus the event sent by a registration and by the buttons of `/admin/encontros`), `billing-jobs` (settlement, maintenance, the end-of-term notice), `newsletter-jobs` (one step per batch of 100), `maintenance-jobs` (event rollup, purges, staged uploads), `lead-jobs`, `admin-jobs`. Schedules are listed in `docs/DEPLOY.md` ("E-mails e jobs").
- **Billing notices** go through `lib/billing-notices.ts` and never throw: by the time one runs the database is already right, and a webhook that failed on a bell would be replayed by the provider and reconcile the whole event again (`docs/BILLING.md`, "Avisos ao integrante").
- **Auth e-mails** (confirmation, password recovery, e-mail change) are sent by Supabase, not by the app: `supabase/templates/*.html`, bilingual by the `locale` the sign-up writes in the account's metadata. They are not rendered by any test here; `docs/DEPLOY.md` has the manual check.

## Auth

- Supabase through `@flyee/auth` (`client`/`server`/`middleware`/`service`). `src/middleware.ts` refreshes the session and protects everything except the public pages (`matchPublicPath`, from `src/i18n/routing.ts`) and `PUBLIC_PREFIXES`. Without `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`/`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` the middleware no-ops and the auth screens show a configuration hint.
- 2FA (TOTP): enrolled at `/settings/security`; the middleware forces the AAL2 step-up at `/auth/two-factor`.
- Internal redirects go through `lib/safe-next.ts` (`sanitizeInternalNext`), never a raw `next` parameter.
- **CLI token server** (`lib/oauth/*`, `docs/CLI-CONTRACT.md`): one first-party public client, `flyee-cli`, seeded in migration 0010; no dynamic registration. Browser login with PKCE and a loopback redirect on any port (`lib/oauth/redirect.ts`), device authorization (`/api/oauth/device` + `/ativar`, `lib/oauth/device-code.ts`), revocation (`/api/oauth/revoke`). Opaque tokens, one family per machine (`device_id`), access 1 h, refresh 30 days rotated on every use: an expired refresh answers `invalid_grant` with `error_uri` = `/revalidar`, and a login on a machine that held a chain before renders the revalidation screen. Logins, revalidations and expired refreshes are product events (`cli.login`, `token.revalidated`, `update.denied_token_expired`).
- **Delivery API** (`app/api/cli/*`): every handler runs inside `runCliRequest` (`lib/cli/gates.ts`), which checks token → scope → `org_entitlements` (read on every call) → `X-Flyee-Device` → `cli_rate_allowance`, answers refusals as `{ error, message (member's language, lib/cli/messages.ts), action_url }` and files each call in `cli_requests`. Downloads are 300-second signed URLs from the private `modules` bucket; the CLI verifies size and SHA-256. Catalog reads live in `lib/catalog/read.ts`, shared with the member dashboard.
- **Packages**: `lib/catalog/package.ts` inspects a ZIP (safe paths, size ceilings, manifest `files` equal to the archive); `lib/catalog/upload.ts` turns a staged upload into a draft version; `lib/catalog/version-actions.ts` publishes, marks stable and yanks (superadmin, audited).

## Commands (run from the monorepo root)

- `npm run dev` — dev server. `npm run build` — production build. `npm run typecheck` — TypeScript 5.8 pinned to this app.
- `npm run test:web` — vitest. `npm run test:e2e` / `npm run test:a11y` — Playwright against a production build (`e2e/baseline.spec.ts`).
- `npm run lint:fix` / `npm run prettier` — lint and formatting.

## Watch out

- `src/style/global.css` imports tokens from `@flyee/design-tokens/css/*`; never recreate tokens locally.
- Deploys go ONLY through GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`: `vercel pull/build/deploy --prebuilt`); the Vercel Git integration stays disconnected. Runbook: `docs/DEPLOY.md`.
- Server-only secrets (`DATABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, provider keys) never reach client components.
- `apps/web/.env` holds inherited MedChina production credentials and `apps/web/.env.local` blanks them; keep `.env.local` until the flyee.club services exist (root `CLAUDE.md`, "Safety during the transition").

===== .claude/rules/app-ux.md =====

---
paths: ["apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/**", "apps/web/src/components/product/**"]

# Product (authenticated app) UX

- The `product-screen` skill is MANDATORY for any create/edit here — a `PreToolUse` hook (`.claude/hooks/product-screen-guard.mjs`) loads it automatically; you never wait to be asked.
- **Goal, not table**: design from the user's job and what success looks like. Never default to a CRUD table of rows — that shape is allowed only when the job really is scan/compare/manage many rows.
- **Never a blank screen**: every zero-data view uses `EmptyState` (icon + why + the ONE next action). A brand-new user must find a path to value (the aha moment).
- Long setups use `SetupWizard` (progressive disclosure); steps to first result use `OnboardingChecklist` + `@flyee/onboarding` (state only; step definitions live in the project's code).
- **Engagement**: completion drive (`ActivationProgress`) and competence feedback only. Never ship points, badges, leaderboards or streaks — documented failures, and streaks carry regulatory risk.
- MUI v9 + theme tokens only, next-intl for every string, inline form errors near the field, skeletons that reserve space.
- **Semantic fields**: phone, CPF/CNPJ, CEP and money never go in a raw `TextField` — use `components/product/fields/*` (mask + check-digit validation + CEP auto-fill via `@flyee/fields`); persist `onlyDigits()`, never the masked string.

===== .claude/rules/design-tokens.md =====

---
paths: ["packages/design-tokens/**", "apps/web/src/style/**"]

# Design tokens

- `packages/design-tokens/css/*.css` is the source of truth for visual identity. `src/tokens.generated.ts` is GENERATED — never edit it manually.
- After any change in `css/*.css`, run `npm run tokens:generate` at the root and include the generated file in the same commit.
- Color values are bare HSL triplets (`191 100% 46%`), consumed via `hsl(var(--token))` in CSS. Keep this format; do not introduce hex/rgb.
- Every color token must exist in light/dark pairs (`:root`/`.dark` in common, `.theme-x`/`.theme-x.dark` in theme files).

===== .claude/rules/icons.md =====

---
paths: ["apps/web/src/icons/**", "apps/web/src/app/**"]

# Icon contract

- Pages import icons only as `@/icons/nexture/ni-*` (the alias may be remapped per project to an adapter set — see `apps/web/src/icons/README.md`). Never import an icon library (Phosphor, Lucide, MUI icons for decoration) directly in a page.
- Every icon component implements `NextureIconsProps` (`size`, `variant`, `className`, `oneTone`) and is a default export. The props type and the size helpers live in `src/icons/nexture-icons.ts`, which imports NO icon (every icon file imports it).
- `src/icons/icon-registry.tsx` (`IconMap`, `NextureIcons`) maps names to components and imports the whole set. Use it only where the icon name is data (the dashboard menu, a catalog icon typed by the operator); a client component that imports it ships every icon to the browser.
- Alternative sets live in sibling folders (`src/icons/phosphor/`, ...) with identical file names; gaps are filled by `npm run icons:stubs -w @flyee/web` (fallback re-exports, never overwritten).
- Adapters import icon libs from their SSR-safe entry (e.g. `@phosphor-icons/react/dist/ssr`) so they work in Server Components.

===== .claude/rules/marketing.md =====

# Marketing layer boundaries

- **One design system.** Every public page (the home, the institutional pages and the campaign pages in `app/[locale]/(funil)/`) composes the primitives in `apps/web/src/components/marketing/`: `Section`/`Container`/`SectionHeader` plus the archetypes listed in `catalog.json`. Never hand-tuned per-page spacing or widths, never a parallel stylesheet vocabulary. The inherited MedChina "Landing DS" was removed on 2026-09-30.
- The `marketing-page` skill is MANDATORY for any create/edit/add-section under `app/[locale]/(marketing)`, `app/[locale]/(funil)` or `components/marketing`. The `PreToolUse` hook (`.claude/hooks/marketing-guard.mjs`) loads it automatically on Write/Edit in all three, and the `PostToolUse` lint (`.claude/hooks/marketing-lint.mjs`) checks every written file there. A file changed by a script bypasses both hooks: load the skill yourself and run the lint on it by hand.
- The committed visual direction lives in `docs/DESIGN.md` and is STRICT: new pages, edits and new sections INHERIT it. Never re-run the direction engine or restyle the UI unless the user explicitly asks for a "redesign". Adding a section triggers a whole-page coherence pass so all sections stay aesthetically aligned.
- **Locales are in the path** (phase 7.1): Portuguese at the root (`/planos`), English under `/en` with translated addresses (`/en/pricing`). Every public page lives under `app/[locale]/` in a folder named after its Portuguese (internal) path, and is declared in `apps/web/src/i18n/routing.ts` (`pathnames`) with both addresses. That declaration is also what makes the middleware treat it as public: there is no separate list of public pages. Only the public site is routed this way; sign-in, the member area, checkout and the admin keep the visitor's cookie/profile language and have no locale in the URL.
- Internal links on public surfaces go through `LocaleLink` (`components/marketing/locale-link.tsx`, also as MUI's `LinkComponent`) or `localizeHref`: `href` is the internal Portuguese path, the link renders the address of the language being read. Links to `/auth/*` and other non-public routes pass through unchanged.
- An INDEXED page also goes to `apps/web/src/app/sitemap.ts`, which emits it once per language with hreflang alternates. A `noindex` page (the campaign pages in `(funil)`, `/fundadores`, `/verificar/[ref]`) stays out of the sitemap and is named in its exclusion comment. Indexing is decided by `metadata` + `sitemap.ts`, never by the route group.
- `/ajuda` and `/blog` are DB-managed: content is written in `/admin/help` / `/admin/blog` and fetched through `apps/web/src/lib/public-content.ts` (anon client, published rows). An address in a language serves content written in that language, never a fallback; translations are separate rows linked by `translation_group`, each with its own slug. The public catalog (`/catalogo`, `/catalogo/[slug]`, the numbers of the home) reads published modules through `apps/web/src/lib/catalog/public.ts` under the same rule: a module whose name has no English text stays out of the English pages and the English sitemap, and a catalog that could not be read is never shown as an empty one. Markdown renders via `components/marketing/markdown-prose.tsx`. Never interpolate DB content as raw HTML.
- SEO is part of every page, per `docs/SEO.md`: exactly one `<h1>` (the page title: `SectionHeader as="h1"` / `PricingSection headingAs="h1"` when the lead is not a `<Hero>`), a localized title + description via `generateMetadata` that spreads `publicPageMetadata({ path, locale })` from `lib/seo.ts` (canonical, hreflang with `x-default`, Open Graph URL and locale), and structured data through `<JsonLd>` (`components/marketing/json-ld.tsx`), never a hand-written `<script>`. `Organization`/`FAQPage`/`Product` schemas are already emitted by the layout/`Faq`/`PricingSection`; do not duplicate them. Inner pages add `BreadcrumbJsonLd`. A missing page answers a real 404 and a moved one a real redirect: never put a loading boundary (`loading.tsx`, or a `<Suspense>` around the children of a layout) above a public page, because the response would start before `notFound()` or `redirect()` runs and go out as a 200.
- Marketing copy lives in the `marketing` i18n namespace, in BOTH locale files (`pt-BR`, `en`), campaign pages included. No hardcoded strings. The home's structured copy lives in `components/marketing/home-copy/{pt-BR,en}.ts`, with `pt-BR.ts` as the structural source of truth (TypeScript refuses the build when `en.ts` drifts). Emphasis is inline (`**em**`, `__strong__`, `==mark==`, `\n`), rendered by `home-copy/rich.tsx`; never put JSX in a copy file. The home's text follows `docs/HOME-COPY.md`, the copy the product owner delivered (committed as delivered): what it asks and the platform cannot back stays out of the page and goes to the owner as a decision.
- **Blocking on every public page**: exactly one `<h1>`, real `alt` text, no fabricated testimonials, metrics or logos, prices and limits read from data (`plans`), honest scarcity (any counter or deadline derives from server state, such as `founders_offer()`), and no claim that the club spends AI credit on the member's behalf.
- **The free rung is never advertised.** No public page or campaign page offers a free plan or a free account, shows a "grátis"/"free" badge on an app, or lists a free column in pricing: the account with no purchase is reached only through content links (`?origem=…&utm_campaign=…`) and the installer's message, and it installs only the entry version of each app (decision of 2026-10-06, `docs/PRODUCT.md`). The one allowed "free" is the waitlist FAQ saying the list itself costs nothing.
- **Copy rules** (the home brief, decided 2026-10-07, `docs/PRODUCT.md`): no dash (— or –), no exclamation mark and no emoji in any visible text, `alt` and `aria-label` included (© and → stay, on purpose), and none of the banned words: desbloqueie, potencialize, sem esforço, soluções inovadoras; unlock, elevate, empower, seamless, robust, supercharge, game-changing, "it's not just". Where a dash would go, write a colon, a comma or a new sentence; separate items with "·"; a missing value hides its line instead of printing a placeholder. The rule covers the member area, the e-mails, the bell and the CLI's messages too; `lib/i18n/copy-rules.test.ts`, pgTAP `0033_copy_rules` and the e2e text check fail when a mark comes back.
- **Colour on text**: under the provisional palette no hue reaches 4.5:1 as small text on a light ground, so hues go on icons, bars and fills while the words keep text colours (`docs/DESIGN.md`, palette usage). The shared components follow it; a page must too.
- Motion is CSS first: the hero entrance and `Float` are CSS animations, `Reveal` is a CSS transition started by `watchEntry` (one shared IntersectionObserver in `components/marketing/motion.ts`), `CountUp` is a short frame loop. GSAP is loaded by `Parallax` alone, on demand. Never add a scripted timeline or a ScrollTrigger to a page, and never an animation without an end. Transform + opacity only, honoring `prefers-reduced-motion`. Never import GSAP in admin code.
- Site identity (name, tagline, siteUrl, favicons) comes from `apps/web/src/brand.ts`; the logo is the single component `components/logo/logo.tsx`.
- **Measurement is declared, never a new tracker.** A click worth measuring carries `data-track="<event>"` and `data-track-<prop>` attributes (or `trackAttributes()` from `lib/site-events.ts` on a link built in code), a section worth measuring passes `track="<key>"` to `Section` or the component that wraps one, and the one listener in `MarketingAnalytics` reports them to GA4 and the Pixel. The vocabulary is the one in `docs/TRACKING.md` ("Site events"): add to it there before using a new name. Never add PostHog or any other tracker, never write site events to the database, and never read the segment from anywhere but `lib/site-segment.ts`.

===== .claude/rules/web-boundaries.md =====

# apps/web boundaries

- `apps/web` is the only app in this repo. Code shared between the app and tooling lives in `packages/*`.
- Do not redefine theme tokens locally (`--primary`, `--grey-*` etc.) — they come from `@flyee/design-tokens`.
- This repo is the flyee.club PLATFORM. The product (the `npx flyee` CLI, the harness core, the module contents) is a separate project: here, it only exists as the API contract (`/api/cli/*`) and the module manifest schema it consumes. Never add product logic to this repo.
